Civic Reasoning Bulletin

Tone Words · The Register in Three Signals
01Procedural

The study's transferable principle is that procedures should look executable: every method has a label, every example has an identifier, every review result becomes a recorded rule. Numbered steps on a fine vertical process line and pointed ribbon labels make the method repeatable without rereading. The pages don't describe a method — they run one.

02Municipal

The study names its associations directly: municipal bulletins, transit signage, election guides, civil-service manuals, examination packets, public-library handouts. The identity carries institutional confidence without looking corporate or luxurious — public-facing, issued, organized for everyone. The exact register for briefing this navy-and-brass civic field.

03Wayfinding

The signature behavior is moving a reader through a process: numbered steps that function as navigation, ribbons that mark changes, a repeated spatial sequence — title band → rule → metadata → content → footer — that the viewer learns once and trusts everywhere. You always know where you are and what comes next.

Section 02 · Design Philosophy

Procedures Should Look Executable

—"GT Five-Step Blind Review — Blue · Red,"a browser-based production file containing a seven-page, letter-size printable training packet with page-selection and export controls — into a complete civic information system for GermaineTutoring.com.

Every page of the source is a station in the same procedure: a full-width navy header with a red rule and gold maker line opens the five-step process; pages 2–4 run two-column worked examples (LSAT question left, numbered blind-review walkthrough right); page 5 converts outcomes into a results table and four-column wrong-answer journal; pages 6–7 distill reviewed questions into portable rules in compact rule blocks.

Principle I

Make the method runnable

The design's job is not to admire a method but to make it runnable: numbered steps, short labels, and direct instructions should make the method easy to repeat without rereading the whole page. Condensed display creates hierarchy without occupying extra width and is reserved for short titles, ribbons, labels, metadata, and process names.

Principle II

One dark ink, one active accent

Navy supplies structure; red identifies action, section changes, and selected emphasis; gold stays secondary and must not carry small body text or primary button labels. White and cool gray form the reading field, navy the institutional weight, red the signal, brass the detail — the discipline that produces a bulletin rather than a generic corporate palette.

Principle III

Condensed display for hierarchy, neutral sans for trust

Instructional prose must remain visually neutral — the body family supports long LR and RC explanations, answer analysis, quotations, punctuation, and conditional notation without ever performing. The contrast between large condensed display and calm explanatory prose is the theme's single strongest character trait.

Principle IV

The paper metaphor appears only where it helps

The direction already sits between a digital application and a paper resource. The website keeps procedural clarity and removes fixed-page behavior from ordinary pages; printable resources retain the full page-preview language and are the theme's strongest extension. The browser workspace and export controls are production tools and stay outside the public visual identity.

Principle V

Civic without seals

Borrow civic architecture's proportions and signage discipline rather than literal columns, seals, or government imagery. Materials stay flat and modern — smooth white stock, cool gray forms, matte navy ink, flat red spot color, thin brass rules — with an explicit ban on beige paper fields, faux aging, heavy grain, and gloss. Photography, when used, is documentary: cool light, dark clothing, white walls, straight-on composition.

How It Communicates with the Viewer

Confidence Through Structure

  1. 1
    Emotional register

    "The student should feel that every task has a defined place and every review decision can be converted into a repeatable action." The site reads the way a well-designed examination bulletin reads: someone rigorous organized this, the process is legible, and following it is within my power. The imagined environment is an LSAT reasoning lab organized like a public information studio.

  2. 2
    The spatial sequence teaches itself

    Full-width navy title bands open sections; a thin red rule separates; compact metadata labels identify; a white or cool-gray field carries the work; horizontal divisions separate the stages. The viewer learns this rhythm on the first page and trusts it everywhere — the same discipline that makes transit signage readable at speed. On mobile it stacks: 38–54px headlines, 16–18px body, stacked metadata.

  3. 3
    Action is always color-coded and labeled

    Bulletin red marks where the viewer can act; navy anchors the frame; gold whispers provenance. Because red never appears as a large background, every red element reads as a signal. Correct/incorrect and confidence states carry text or icon redundancy — red and green alone cannot carry meaning.

  4. 4
    The two-column worked example is the signature teaching gesture

    Question on the left, numbered blind-review on the right, narrow divider between — the viewer watches the method execute rather than reading a lecture about it. On narrow screens the vertical process line disappears rather than crowding the copy; the numbers alone preserve the sequence.

  5. 5
    Public-facing and accessible, never luxurious

    Brand personality: serious, useful, accessible, prepared, decisive, student-centered. Pricing renders as a structured ledger, testimonials pair a condensed score label with a plain-language quote. The viewer is a citizen of this system, not a prospect being sold to.

Section 03 · Color System

Navy Carries, Red Signals, Brass Whispers

White and cool gray create the reading field; navy carries the institutional weight; red marks action and section changes; gold appears in small amounts as provenance and detail.

#0D2F50
Ink Navy
Primary brand field — titles, navigation, header and footer bands, primary ink. Carries the institutional weight. Full-width bands only, never whole-page backgrounds.
#9E3030
Bulletin Red
Section ribbons, active controls, separators, selected emphasis, focus highlights, interactive badges. The action signal — thin and pointed, never a field.
#BFA168
Brass Gold
Maker text, selected numerals, small dividers, premium detail. Keep out of small body text and primary buttons. Strictly ornamental — a token-level constraint, not a guideline.
#FFFFFF
Paper White
Primary site and document background; the long reading surface. Default field for ordinary site pages.
#F0F3F6
Cool Form Gray
Answer boxes, tables, metadata strips, alternate sections, light cards, container tint. The second reading field.
#333333
Carbon Text
Primary prose, answer choices, table text. The quiet workhorse that lets navy, red, and gold stay signals.
Tonal Logic

Reading field → weight → signal → detail

#0D2F50, Active Accent / Signal #9E3030, and Companion Tint / Light #F0F3F6. Red is reserved for action and transition, always at small scale; because it never appears as a large background, every red element reads as a signal.

Accessibility rule: correct/incorrect, accuracy, confidence, and status states are built with text and icon redundancy, not color alone — red and green cannot carry meaning by themselves. Calls to action run navy or bulletin-red buttons with clear secondary-sans labels; gold never carries primary button text.
Materials: matte and flat — smooth white stock, cool gray forms, matte navy ink, flat red spot color, thin brass rules, occasional stamped labels. No beige paper fields, no faux aging, no heavy grain, no gloss.
Section 04 · Typography System

Condensed Authority Over Neutral Prose

Oswald + Inter — but that pair is assigned to the sibling Varsity Study Fieldbook study, whose final PDF embeds it directly, so family-level exclusivity removes both from this direction. All ten families below are The five tested pairs, shown in their actual fonts:

1Big Shoulders Display + DM SansBest Overall Website System
The Architecture of Sufficient Assumption Standardized legal reasoning requires rigorous logical decomposition. When evaluating an argument, separate premises from subsidiary conclusions before testing the validity of conditional inferences — PT 84 · S 2 · Q 14, 78% of preparers miss the (→) chain.

Roles & Character

Primary: Big Shoulders Display Semibold/Bold for heroes, resource titles, step names, campaign covers. Secondary: DM Sans Regular/Medium for explanations; Semibold for navigation, controls, table headers.

Character: city design office meets modern LSAT method lab. Strength: the clearest translation of the source's civic energy into a distinct website identity — genuine civic-design association and the tall American Gothic structure visible in the source.

Weakness & Discipline

Big Shoulders can dominate below title size — keep it out of paragraph text and ordinary controls, and reserve only the weights and branch used (the family spans Display, Text, Stencil, Inline).

Sources: · googlefonts/dm-fonts.

Behavior Rules · From the Study
  • ARole split. Display family: heroes, resource titles, section labels, step names, package names, campaign covers. Body family: navigation, buttons, explanations, answer choices, annotations, confidence labels, tables, mobile interface text.
  • BKeep condensed headings short. Wrap to preserve recognizable word shapes; never stack one-word lines.
  • CBody copy runs 16–18px with 1.5–1.65 line height for dense explanations.
  • DTabular numerals wherever score tables, question identifiers, and timing data need stable alignment.
  • ETest before launch: parentheses, quotation marks, arrows, slashes, percent signs, and PT/S/Q identifiers in both families.
  • FDisplay authority without costume — no drift into sports branding, novelty poster type, or military stencil language. Body must distinguish I / l / 1 cleanly with open counters, reliable numerals, stable punctuation, several useful weights.
Section 07 · Assessment Ledger

Risks, Open Questions

Risks

  • Government costume — literal columns, seals, and insignia are banned, but a heavy hand with brass, ribbons, or navy bands could still read as parody of a permit office rather than a disciplined bulletin.
  • Every pair has a known failure mode — Big Shoulders dominates below title size; Yanone Kaffeesatz carries café nostalgia; Alegreya Sans may feel literary in dense tables; Encode Sans + Lato risks blandness. Production discipline must manage whichever wins.
  • Mobile is subtraction work — pointed ribbons, vertical process lines, and fixed-page geometry degrade quickly; the study repeatedly instructs removal before awkward wrapping.
  • Gold's small-scale-only rule is easy to violate — charts, badges, and dividers proliferate; it needs a token-level constraint, not a guideline.
  • A lot of system for a small team — dense tables plus condensed display plus navy bands must stay consistent across website, portal, printables, and social.

Open Questions

  • The five-system comparison test is unbuilt — identical content and spacing across hero, navigation, one long LR/RC page, one five-step module, one results table and journal entry, one pricing section, one biography/testimonial module, and one 390px resource page; scored on display character, long-form comfort, mobile rendering, table clarity, numeral/punctuation quality, accessibility, page weight, and navy-red-gold fit. First heat: pair 1 vs. pair 2, with pair 5 as the expressive boundary case.
  • Which Saira width and weight recipe gets locked if pair 2 wins — the family is too broad to ship unsubsetted.
  • How much of the export behavior becomes a real product feature in the student portal (print, vertical image, grid image, per-page images) rather than remaining a production convenience.
  • Whether the brass maker line survives as personalization
  • Whether photography enters the system at all — crisp documentary desk scenes and portraits are permitted, but the identity is strong enough typographically to run image-free.

PT 84 · S 2 · Q 14Sufficient Assumption — Worked Example
Stimulus
"Whenever the council adopts a transit measure without a funding plan, implementation stalls. The council adopted the Riverline measure, and implementation did not stall. Therefore…"
AThe Riverline measure included a funding plan.
BThe Riverline measure was not adopted without a funding plan. ✓ selected
CSome adopted measures stall despite funding plans.
DThe council rarely adopts transit measures.
Blind Review Walkthrough
  1. 1Stimulus analysis. Map the conditional: no funding plan → stalls. Contrapositive: did not stall → funding plan existed.
  2. 2Prephrase. The conclusion needs the contrapositive applied to Riverline before looking at choices.
  3. 3Answer justification. (B) restates the prephrase exactly — the missing link, fully sufficient.
  4. 4Removal rationale. (A) is a shell: "included a plan" ≠ the conditional chain the argument requires.
